reedling.text: A quick little river fish that bites all year, and the first catch most new anglers make.

brookslip.text: A spring fish of the shallows that darts away from the bait the moment it feels a tug.

millrun.text: Runs up the river in summer and likes the warm shallows near the mill.

ferrywhisker.text: A whiskered bottom feeder that lurks near the old ferry landing in autumn, day or night.

salmon.text: The big autumn run. Salmon fight hard and sell well, and the Stream Fish bundle asks for them.

hearthside-dace.text: Rises at dusk all year, when the lamps in the valley come on.

tallow-eel.text: A pale, slippery eel that only bites on winter nights, down near the river bed.

silverthread.text: A flash of silver at first light. Rare, and quick to slip the line.

old-mossback.text: An old fish with a mossy back that stirs on rainy autumn days. It sinks and then pulls.

carp.text: The steady fish of the forest lake. It bites in daylight in every season.

perch.text: A spring perch, easy enough to land with a decent rod.

fernfin.text: Named for its green, frilled fins. It comes to the forest lake in summer.

mushroom-loach.text: A dusk-time loach of the forest lake in autumn, found near the damp, mushroomy banks.

moonmirror.text: Rises on any night, when the forest lake is flat and still.

hermit-trout.text: A shy trout that only shows itself while it rains.

marshlight.text: A pale fish of the delta marsh lake that drifts about in the daytime.

bogwhisker.text: A darting fish of the marsh lake in spring and summer.

sunk-boot-loach.text: Often hooked when an angler expected something grander. It bites at any hour.

reed-cat.text: A night-time fish of the reeds that keeps low and moves slowly.

catfish.text: A dusk fish of the marsh lake. It sinks, and rarely gives up quickly.

bullhead.text: A grumpy bottom fish that bites in the marsh lake when it rains.

glassy-elver.text: A see-through young eel of the marsh lake, caught at dawn in spring.

sardine.text: A small silver fish found along the coast in daylight, all year.

skiff-sprat.text: A tiny fish that gathers around the boats at the Beach every day of the year.

mackerel.text: A fast, smooth swimmer of the Beach in summer and autumn.

mullet.text: Comes to the shallows at dawn in spring.

cod.text: The winter staple of the coast, caught in daylight.

kelp-ribbon.text: A long, ribbon-like fish that floats among the kelp at dusk.

harbour-ray.text: A flat ray that glides into the Beach shallows in summer.

herring.text: Silver shoals come in at night all year round.

lantern-squid.text: A glowing squid of autumn and winter nights. It rises, then drifts.

crowned-tunny.text: A rare, fast-swimming tunny that visits the sea in summer and autumn, by day.

cold-quill.text: A spiny little fish of the mountain lake, found by day in every season.

arctic-char.text: Likes the cold: winter and spring in the mountain lake.

granite-gudgeon.text: A grey fish of the rocky bottom, caught at any hour of the day or night.

echo-pike.text: A pike that strikes when rain rings across the mountain lake.

ember-trout.text: A trout with an orange belly, seen at dusk on summer evenings.

glacier-ghost.text: A pale giant that drifts through the mountain lake on winter nights. Rare.

pearlback.text: A shimmering fish of the lake cove, found in the daytime.

cove-lantern.text: A glowing fish of the lake cove after dark.

still-water-gar.text: A long-snouted gar that waits in the still cove waters in spring and summer.

velvet-koi.text: A rare, deep-coloured koi that surfaces in the cove at dusk in autumn.

hush.text: A rare fish of the cove that comes at dawn. It makes no splash at all.

dusk-opal.text: A rare fish of the cove that gleams at dusk, whatever the season.

deepglow.text: A rare, softly glowing fish of the cove on winter nights.

shell-ghost.text: A rare fish of the cove that only appears when it rains.

hearthwell-carp.text: A legend. An enormous carp, said to live in the lake cove. Catch it at dusk in autumn, in the rain.

grandmother-hush.text: A legend. A huge old fish of the forest lake, kin to the cove's Hush. Catch it at dusk in spring, in the rain.

valley-king.text: A legend. The king of the river. Catch it at dawn in autumn, in the rain.

moonlit-mother.text: A legend. A pale giant char of the mountain lake. Catch it on a clear winter night.

great-hearthfin.text: A legend. A huge sea fish, and the one legend that bites in any weather. Catch it by day in summer.
